title: Higher-order components: wrap a component to add props

slides.say: Before Hooks, React code shared logic with higher-order components. You'll still meet them in older code.
A higher-order component is a function that takes a component and returns a new one. This one renders the original and adds a user prop. It passes every other prop through.
Never call it inside a component. Each render makes a brand new component type, so React remounts it and its state is lost. Wrap once, outside.
Today, a custom Hook does the same job with less wrapping. The component just calls use user.

slides.text: HOCs are rare in modern React. Prefer custom Hooks; recognize HOCs in older libraries.
slides.say: So prefer custom Hooks for new code, and recognize higher-order components when a library hands you one.
